definition: The quantity you choose and change on purpose in an experiment, to see what effect it has.
The quantity you measure in an experiment, to see how it changes when the independent variable changes.
A quantity that could also affect the dependent variable, so it is kept the same for every reading to make the test fair.
The smallest and largest values of a variable in an experiment, such as distances from 20 cm to 70 cm.
An experiment is valid if it tests what it says it tests: it is a fair test in which only the independent and dependent variables change and the control variables stay the same.
